role: First list-price entry for gpt-6-astra, now that OpenAI publishes an official rate card. Used to value each plan's adopted monthly Astra allowance at metered API rates (the api_cost_usd_month column).
roleZh: gpt-6-astra 首个标价档案：OpenAI 现已公布官方三段价，用于把各套餐的采用月额度按 API 标价折算成美元成本（api_cost_usd_month 列）。

priceTiers.official: First-party vendor pricing page read this round. High confidence.
priceTiers.official_indirect: First-party rate restated in vendor docs, announcement or console help because the pricing page itself is JS-rendered or gives no three-part split. Medium confidence.
priceTiers.third_party: Open-weight or wrapper-only model with no first-party rate card; a named gateway or tracker rate is recorded instead. Low confidence.
priceTiers.unavailable: No defensible public rate found. Prices stay null and the API cost column stays blank; no value is invented.

conventions.regionRule: Where a vendor publishes both an international and a domestic-CNY list, the international USD list is recorded as the base, matching the existing qwen3.7-plus decision.
conventions.promoRule: Base fields hold the standing list price; promotional and speed/context variants stay in variants and are not used for the API cost column.
conventions.cacheFallback: cachedInput null means the vendor publishes no cache-read rate; compute.py falls back to 0.1x input, which is the multiplier every vendor that does publish one uses.
conventions.blendRule: The API cost column weights cachedInput/input/output by the project standard workload in conventions.json (97.5% / 2.15% / 0.35%). Cache writes are still not modeled, so API cost is a floor for providers that bill them.

cacheWrite.note: Cache writes billed separately: standard short 12.5, long 25, batch/flex 6.25, fast 25/50. Not modeled in the API cost column, so computed API cost is a floor.

models.note: New this round. First official rate card; short-context Standard rates used as base. Priority processing renamed Fast mode on 2026-07-30. Verified live against the pricing page today.

unpricedRationale: Speed/Fast tiers inside wrapper products and wrapper-exclusive models have no separately published metered rate. Their API cost column stays blank; the subscription rows themselves are unaffected.
